implementation_notes: In C the blob is not a class but a set of globals plus a handful of functions in one translation unit, with everything else calling into it — the procedural controller wrapped in a struct, or not even wrapped. The diagnosis is the same usage map, computed with `ctags` or by grepping each global's name, and the extraction is a new translation unit per cluster with a narrow header declaring only what the cluster exposes. The C-specific reason this matters is load cost: a blob's state has to be initialised for any operation, which in C means a constructor function everybody calls.
idiom_name: one translation unit of globals plus a main loop
pitfalls: Global state in a header (`extern`) means any translation unit can couple to any cluster; the fix is narrowing the declarations, not just moving code.
A `main()` that initialises every global before doing anything is the C blob's constructor problem in its clearest form.
Static analysis reports on functions well and on globals poorly, so the usage map has to be built by hand or with a tag tool.
